decisions: Translated the Postgres unique-violation for UQ_identity_auth_identities_provider_identifier into DomainError.conflict('phone_already_exists', ...) inside TypeOrmAuthIdentityRepository.save() (new private translateUniqueViolation helper), instead of a DB advisory lock, SELECT ... FOR UPDATE, or a retry loop — the finding was about the reported status code being wrong for the race's loser, not about data integrity (the unique index and transaction rollback already prevented any duplicate row or partial state).

Matched on both Postgres SQLSTATE 23505 and the exact constraint name (not SQLSTATE alone or message text), because auth_identities has a second unique index (UQ_identity_auth_identities_provider_subject, for social-provider subject) that also raises 23505 for an unrelated conflict — matching only on SQLSTATE would have mislabeled that as phone_already_exists too.

Fixed at the repository level (not inside CreateAccountUseCase specifically) because ChangeAccountPhoneUseCase has the identical TOCTOU preflight-check shape and calls the same authIdentities.save(); a repository-level fix closes the race for both call sites without touching either use case.

Added the concurrency regression test to the existing 'register (changes/cycle-002 addendum)' describe block in apps/api/test/auth-flow.e2e-spec.ts (real Postgres, two genuinely concurrent HTTP requests) rather than a mocked-repository unit test — the bug is specifically about real concurrent DB writes, which a mock can't exercise; no TypeOrm*Repository in this codebase has its own unit-test file, so this also matches established convention.

Did not touch RegisterUseCase, CreateAccountUseCase, ChangeAccountPhoneUseCase, AuthController, GlobalExceptionFilter, or any already-passed slice/criterion — scoped exactly to fix-request-review-3.md's one major finding.

notes: This attempt's (attempt 5) net-new work was narrow: review cycle 3 (codex) returned exactly one major finding — AC46's preflight duplicate-phone check is TOCTOU-racy under real concurrency, so the loser of two simultaneous registrations for the same phone got a generic 500 instead of the required 409 business error, even though the transaction itself still rolled back correctly (no partial/duplicate state was ever actually created — only the reported status code was wrong).

Fix is entirely in the infrastructure layer: TypeOrmAuthIdentityRepository.save() now catches the database's own unique-constraint violation and translates it into the same DomainError.conflict the preflight check already throws for the non-racy case, so GlobalExceptionFilter maps it to 409 as before.
